class.name: MediaSource
class.brief_description: Reads a media file (Matroska/WebM, MP4/MOV, MPEG-TS, AVI) with FFmpeg: video access units for a hardware decoder, decoded audio for an [AudioStreamMedia].
class.description: Opens a file with FFmpeg's libavformat and reads it on a worker thread. The video stream is only demuxed: its access units go, in Annex-B for H.264 and HEVC (converted from MP4/Matroska's length-prefixed form with the [code]h264_mp4toannexb[/code] / [code]hevc_mp4toannexb[/code] bitstream filters), through a bounded queue to a [V4L2Decoder] ([method V4L2Decoder.open_source], [method HWVideoTexture.open_source]). The first access unit after [method open] and after every [method seek] is a keyframe with the parameter sets (VPS/SPS/PPS) in band. Files on a file share open by URL: [code]smb://host/share/path/file.mkv[/code] (SMB2/3, see [method set_smb_credentials] and [member network_buffer_size]). A thread of their own reads them ahead into a ring buffer, so network latency doesn't reach the demuxer. Subtitle tracks can be selected too ([method select_subtitle_track], [method read_subtitle_event]): text tracks are decoded to text and ASS lines, bitmap tracks passed through as packets. The selected audio track is decoded and resampled with libswresample to stereo float at the [AudioServer] mix rate, into a ring buffer that [method get_audio_stream] plays. More than two channels are downmixed (centre and surrounds at -3 dB, LFE dropped); the source layout is in [method get_audio_tracks]. The playback position of that stream is the A/V master clock. All times are media seconds: the stream timestamp minus the file's start time ([method get_start_time]), so the first frame is at about 0. The thread blocks when the queues are full ([member video_queue_seconds], [member audio_queue_seconds]) and is woken when they are consumed; it never spins. [codeblock] var source := MediaSource.new() if source.open("/path/film.mkv") == OK: print(source.get_info()) video.open_source(source) # HWVideoTexture $AudioStreamPlayer.stream = source.get_audio_stream() [/codeblock]

method.name: add_external_subtitle
method.description: Loads a subtitle file (SubRip, ASS/SSA or WebVTT; a local path or smb://) as one more subtitle track after the file's own, and returns its index, or -1 if it can't be read ([method get_last_error] says why; the source keeps playing). Blocking: it reads the whole file (up to 16 MiB). Text in UTF-8, UTF-16 with a byte order mark, or anything else read as Windows-1252. [param language] and [param title] default to what the file name says ([method MediaBrowser.parse_subtitle_name]) and the file name. The track is selected like any other; its events are all handed out by [method read_subtitle_event] at once, in time order, and again from the events still showing at the target after a [method seek]. [method close] drops the files. Find the files with [method MediaBrowser.find_subtitles].

method.name: close
method.description: Stops the thread and closes the file. Close a [V4L2Decoder] reading from it first.

method.name: get_audio_position
method.description: Returns the media time of the next audio frame to be mixed: the time of the last frame mixed plus one frame. Right after [method seek] it is the seek target.

method.name: get_audio_stream
method.description: Returns a new [AudioStreamMedia] that plays the decoded audio. Play it from one [AudioStreamPlayer] at a time.

method.name: get_audio_track
method.description: Returns the selected audio track (index into [method get_audio_tracks]), or -1.

method.name: get_bit_rate
method.description: Returns the container's overall bit rate in bit/s (all streams), or 0 if it doesn't say.

method.name: get_chapter_at
method.description: Returns the index of the chapter playing at [param seconds], or -1 before the first chapter, after the last one ends, or when the file has none.

method.name: get_chapters
method.description: Returns the file's chapters (Matroska, MP4): one Dictionary each, [code]index[/code], [code]start[/code], [code]end[/code] (media seconds, like every time here) and [code]title[/code] (may be empty), sorted by start. A chapter without an end lasts until the next one. Empty if the file has none.

method.name: get_audio_tracks
method.description: Returns one Dictionary per audio stream: [code]index[/code], [code]stream_index[/code], [code]codec[/code], [code]channels[/code], [code]channel_layout[/code] (for example "5.1(side)"), [code]sample_rate[/code], [code]bit_rate[/code], [code]language[/code] (as the file says it), [code]language_code[/code] ([method normalize_language]), [code]title[/code], [code]default[/code], [code]commentary[/code] and [code]visual_impaired[/code] (audio description; both from the stream's flags or its title).

method.name: get_duration
method.description: Returns the duration in seconds (0 if unknown).

method.name: get_info
method.description: Returns [code]path[/code], [code]format[/code], [code]duration[/code], [code]start_time[/code], [code]bit_rate[/code], [code]video[/code] ([method get_video_info]), [code]audio_tracks[/code], [code]subtitle_tracks[/code], [code]chapters[/code] ([method get_chapters]), [code]audio_track[/code], [code]subtitle_track[/code] and [code]output_rate[/code].

method.name: get_external_subtitle_count
method.description: Returns how many subtitle files [method add_external_subtitle] has added since [method open].

method.name: get_last_error
method.description: Returns the last error or warning (a failed seek or an audio track that can't be decoded don't stop the source).

method.name: get_output_rate
method.description: Returns the sample rate of the decoded audio: the [AudioServer] mix rate when the file was opened.

method.name: get_path
method.description: Returns the path given to [method open].

method.name: get_position
method.description: Returns [method get_audio_position] if an audio track is selected, else the PTS of the last video access unit taken from the queue.

method.name: get_seek_target
method.description: Returns the target of the last [method seek] (0 after [method open]).

method.name: get_serial
method.description: Returns the seek count. Video access units carry the serial they were read under.

method.name: get_start_time
method.description: Returns the file's start time in seconds, which is subtracted from every timestamp.

method.name: get_state
method.description: Returns the state.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Returns counters: [code]bitrate_bps[/code] (the video bit rate at the playback position, over the last 3 whole seconds with data; left out while unknown, see [method get_video_bitrate_history]), [code]packets_read[/code], [code]bytes_read[/code], [code]video_packets[/code], [code]video_bytes[/code], [code]video_skipped[/code] (before the first keyframe), [code]video_parameter_sets_added[/code], [code]video_queue[/code], [code]video_queue_bytes[/code], [code]audio_packets[/code], [code]audio_frames_out[/code], [code]audio_decode_errors[/code], [code]audio_dropped_frames[/code] (before a seek target), [code]audio_silence_frames[/code], [code]audio_buffered[/code] (seconds), [code]audio_position[/code], [code]audio_underruns[/code] (the ring ran empty during playback), [code]audio_seek_waits[/code] (it was empty before the first frame after open or a seek: expected, the position holds), [code]audio_frames_mixed[/code], [code]audio_finished[/code], [code]read_errors[/code], [code]seeks[/code], [code]seek_retries[/code], [code]subtitle_events[/code], [code]subtitle_decode_errors[/code], [code]subtitle_queue[/code], [code]thread_cpu_seconds[/code] (CPU time of the demux thread), [code]serial[/code], [code]eof[/code], [code]state[/code], [code]state_name[/code], [code]last_error[/code], [code]network[/code] ([code]true[/code] for smb:// files). For smb:// files also: [code]net_buffer_bytes[/code] (ring size), [code]net_buffered_bytes[/code] (read ahead of the demuxer's position), [code]net_bytes_read[/code], [code]net_requests[/code], [code]net_resets[/code] (seeks outside the buffered range), [code]net_waits[/code] (reads that had to wait for the network), [code]net_seek_waits[/code] (of those, waits while the buffer refilled after open or a seek: expected), [code]net_stalls[/code] and [code]net_stall_seconds[/code] (waits once the buffer had refilled: the network didn't keep up), [code]net_wait_seconds[/code], [code]net_refills[/code] (refills done: from open or a seek until 4 MiB were read ahead), [code]net_refill_seconds[/code], [code]net_refill_mbps[/code] (the read rate during refills, which bounds how fast a seek settles: the decoder needs everything from the keyframe before the target), [code]net_reconnects[/code], [code]net_errors[/code], [code]net_read_mbps[/code] (Mbit/s while requests were in flight: the link's rate), [code]net_average_mbps[/code] (since open), [code]net_busy_seconds[/code], [code]net_thread_cpu_seconds[/code] (CPU time of the readahead thread).

method.name: get_subtitle_header
method.description: Returns the ASS header ([code][Script Info][/code], [code][V4+ Styles][/code], [code][Events][/code] format) of the selected text subtitle track, for libass. Empty for bitmap tracks, and until the demux thread has opened the track's decoder.

method.name: get_subtitle_track
method.description: Returns the selected subtitle track, or -1.

method.name: get_subtitle_tracks
method.description: Returns one Dictionary per subtitle stream: [code]index[/code], [code]stream_index[/code], [code]codec[/code], [code]text[/code] (decoded to text: SubRip, ASS/SSA, MP4 timed text, WebVTT), [code]bitmap[/code] (PGS, VobSub, DVB, XSUB: passed through), [code]language[/code], [code]language_code[/code] ([method normalize_language]), [code]title[/code], [code]default[/code], [code]forced[/code], [code]hearing_impaired[/code] (both also from the title), [code]external[/code], and for subtitle files ([method add_external_subtitle]) [code]path[/code]. The file's own tracks come first.

method.name: get_video_bitrate_history
method.description: Returns the video bit rate in kbit/s of each of the [param seconds] whole media seconds before [param at] (the playback position), oldest first, from the sizes of the packets read; -1 where it isn't known (not read since the last [method seek], or more than about 64 s from the read position). At most 64 values. For a bitrate graph; [method HWVideoTexture.get_overlay_stats] includes the last 60 s.

method.name: get_video_info
method.description: Returns the video stream: [code]codec[/code] ("h264", "hevc", "vp9", "av1" or FFmpeg's name), [code]is_h264[/code], [code]is_hevc[/code], [code]is_vp9[/code], [code]is_av1[/code], [code]width[/code], [code]height[/code] (the cropped picture size, before any pixel aspect; the exact visible rectangle comes from [method HWVideoTexture.get_visible_rect]), [code]sample_aspect_ratio[/code] (pixel aspect, 1 if square or unknown), [code]display_aspect[/code], [code]fps[/code], [code]bit_depth[/code], [code]profile[/code], [code]pixel_format[/code], the colour description [code]color_primaries[/code], [code]color_transfer[/code], [code]color_matrix[/code], [code]color_range[/code] (FFmpeg's names such as "bt709", "bt2020nc", "smpte2084", "tv"; empty if unspecified) and from it [code]matrix_bt2020[/code], [code]full_range[/code] and [code]hdr[/code] (PQ or HLG transfer: needs tone mapping), [code]hw_decodable[/code] (the Frame can decode and show it in hardware: H.264 or HEVC, 4:2:0, 8-bit, or 10-bit when the decoder offers P010), [code]hw_unsupported_reason[/code] (why not, as a sentence for the user; empty if it can), [code]software_decodable[/code] (not in hardware, but [HWVideoTexture] decodes it in software: H.264, HEVC or VP9 up to about 1080p), [code]playable[/code] (one or the other), [code]unplayable_reason[/code] (why neither), [code]annexb_filter[/code], and from the SPS [code]coded_width[/code], [code]coded_height[/code], [code]display_width[/code], [code]display_height[/code], [code]chroma_format[/code]. Empty if there is no video. The container's stereo 3D and spherical metadata (Matroska StereoMode and Projection, MP4 st3d and sv3d), empty or zero when it says nothing (then guess from the file name): [code]stereo_mode[/code] ("2d", "sbs", "tb", "frame_sequence", "checkerboard", "sbs_quincunx", "lines", "columns", or "unspecified" when the file says only that it has two views, as Apple's MP4 boxes do), [code]stereo_inverted[/code] (the right eye's picture comes first), [code]stereo_mode_tag[/code] (Matroska's StereoMode as its stream tag, such as "left_right" or "bottom_top"; empty otherwise), [code]stereo_baseline_mm[/code], [code]stereo_fov[/code] (degrees), [code]projection[/code] ("equirectangular", "half_equirectangular", "cubemap", "fisheye", "rectilinear", "parametric_immersive", "other"), [code]projection_fov[/code] (degrees across and down, a [Vector2]: 360x180 for a full equirectangular sphere, 180x180 for VR180, 0 if unknown), [code]projection_yaw_pitch_roll[/code] (degrees, a [Vector3]) and [code]projection_bounds[/code] (the equirectangular crop: left, top, right, bottom as fractions of the full sphere, a [Vector4]).

method.name: read_subtitle_event
method.description: Takes the next event of the selected subtitle track: [code]start[/code] and [code]end[/code] (media seconds; [code]end[/code] is -1 when unknown, as for most bitmap tracks, where the next event ends it), [code]text[/code] (plain text, lines separated by [code]\n[/code], ASS override tags removed), [code]ass[/code] (FFmpeg's ASS event line(s): ReadOrder, Layer, Style, Name, margins, Effect, Text), [code]bitmap[/code], [code]data[/code] (bitmap tracks: the raw packet), [code]serial[/code]. Returns an empty Dictionary when none is queued. Events come in file order, about the queue length ahead of the playback position; keep them until their time. At most 512 are queued (the oldest are dropped). Subtitle files ([method add_external_subtitle]) hand out all their events at once instead. For a negative subtitle delay, see [member subtitle_read_ahead].

method.name: select_subtitle_track
method.description: Selects a subtitle track (-1: none). This doesn't seek: events whose packets were read before (up to the queue length ahead of the playback position) aren't delivered. An event that started before a seek target isn't delivered after the seek either, unless its packet lies after the keyframe the seek lands on.

method.name: is_eof
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] once the file is read to the end (queued data may still be waiting).

method.name: is_open
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] between a successful [method open] and [method close].

method.name: language_name
method.description: Returns the English name of a language code or name, normalized first: [code]"ger"[/code] gives [code]"German"[/code], [code]"pt-BR"[/code] gives [code]"Portuguese (BR)"[/code]. Unknown codes come back as given.

method.name: normalize_language
method.description: Returns the ISO 639-1 code for a language as containers and file names give it: ISO 639-2/B and /T codes ([code]"ger"[/code], [code]"deu"[/code]), ISO 639-1 codes, and English names ([code]"German"[/code]) all give [code]"de"[/code]. Lower case, with a region kept after a hyphen ([code]"pt_BR"[/code] gives [code]"pt-br"[/code]). [code]"und"[/code] and other "no language" codes give an empty string; unknown codes come back lower case.

method.name: open
method.description: Opens a file, reads its stream information, selects the default audio track and starts reading. Blocks while it reads the start of the file. [param path] is a local path, a [code]res://[/code] or [code]user://[/code] path, or [code]smb://host/share/path/file[/code] (not URL-encoded: names are written as they are). For an smb:// file, the host is connected and logged into with the credentials of [method set_smb_credentials] (else as guest), which can take up to about 8 s per step when the host doesn't answer: open from a worker thread if the caller must not stall. Errors are sentences for the user in [method get_last_error], for example "Access denied: HOST refused the user name or password." or "Not found: share/path on HOST.".

method.name: pick_audio_track
method.description: Language memory: returns the audio track that fits [param languages] (codes or names, the most preferred first) best, or -1 if none is in any of them. Among tracks of the same language: not a commentary, not audio description, the default flag, then more channels. A preference without a region matches every region; one with a region matches only that region.

method.name: pick_subtitle_track
method.description: Language memory: returns the subtitle track (the file's own and the added files) that fits [param languages] best, or -1. Among tracks of the same language: text before bitmap (only text is drawn so far), full before forced, without before with hearing-impaired notes, the default flag, the file's own before a file. With [param forced_only], only forced tracks count (the foreign parts of a film whose audio is in the viewer's language).

method.name: read_video_packet
method.description: For scripts and tests: takes the next video access unit from the queue and returns [code]data[/code] (a copy), [code]pts[/code], [code]dts[/code], [code]keyframe[/code], [code]serial[/code], [code]sps_width[/code], [code]sps_height[/code] (coded size of an SPS in it, or 0), [code]nal_type[/code] and [code]random_access[/code] (for keyframes and the first access unit after a seek: the first picture NAL unit type, and "idr", "cra", "bla" or "i" for an H.264 non-IDR I picture; -1 and "" otherwise). Returns an empty Dictionary if none is queued yet. Don't use it while a [V4L2Decoder] reads the same source.

method.name: seek
method.description: Drops everything queued and reads again from the keyframe at or before [param seconds]. Containers without a keyframe index (MPEG-TS) are seeked by timestamp: when the first keyframe found is after the target, the file is seeked again 2, 4, 8... s earlier (up to 6 times; [code]seek_retries[/code] in [method get_stats]), with the audio read meanwhile held back. Decoded audio before the target is dropped (and a short gap filled with silence), so the audio clock restarts exactly at the target. A [HWVideoTexture] playing this source notices the new serial, drops its stale frames and shows the frame at the target. Returns the new serial. Any thread.

method.name: select_audio_track
method.description: Selects an audio track (-1: none). While open, this seeks to the current position, because the queues already hold the old track's audio.

method.name: set_smb_credentials
method.description: Sets the credentials for smb:// files on [param host] (as it appears in the URL; not case-sensitive), shared with [MediaBrowser] ([method MediaBrowser.set_smb_credentials] is the same). [param domain] is the host's computer name or workgroup for a local account, or empty. An empty user and password remove the entry. Kept in memory only; never logged, never part of a path. NTLMSSP authentication; signing is used when the server requires it (AES-CMAC, with the CPU's AES instructions when it has them).

members.member: FFmpeg options for the audio decoder (AVOptions, as strings), applied when a track's decoder opens. For example [code]{"core_only": "1"}[/code] makes the DTS decoder ignore the DTS-HD extensions (XLL lossless, XBR, X96) and decode the core only, as a cheaper fallback. Options a decoder doesn't know are ignored. Set before [method open].
Decoded audio to keep ahead of the playback position. Set before [method open].
If [code]true[/code], the downmix to stereo is scaled so no sum can exceed full scale (about 7.7 dB quieter for 5.1). Set before [method open].

Size in bytes of the readahead ring of smb:// files (4 MiB to 256 MiB; applies at the next [method open]). Reads of up to 1 MiB, up to 4 in flight; 1/8 of the ring is kept behind the read position for short backward seeks, the rest is read ahead. After a seek outside the ring the readahead starts at 256 KiB and doubles as the file is read on. A lost connection is reopened (5 tries, 0.5 s to 8 s apart) and the reading resumes where it stopped; after that the source goes to [constant STATE_ERROR] with the reason in [method get_last_error].
Read requests (of up to 1 MiB) in flight at once for smb:// files, 1 to 16; applies at the next [method open]. More keeps a link with more latency busy.

0.5 to 2. The audio plays faster or slower with its pitch kept (a WSOLA time stretch in the mixer: about 0.3 % of an x86 core at any speed other than 1, nothing at 1), and as the audio clock is the master clock, the video follows; the decoder then has to decode that much faster. Takes effect at the next mix, any time. The output latency corrections of the clock ([method AudioServer.get_time_since_last_mix], [method AudioServer.get_output_latency]) are in real seconds: multiply them by the speed. Without an audio track, set [member HWVideoTexture.playback_speed] instead.

Seconds (0 to 30). The events of a file's own subtitle tracks come with its packets, about [member video_queue_seconds] ahead of the playback. A negative subtitle delay (showing lines earlier) needs them earlier than that: set this to the largest such delay, and while a subtitle track of the file is selected the video is read that far ahead (plus 0.5 s), within the queue's limits of 512 packets and 96 MiB (about 20 s at 24 fps). Costs memory, not CPU. The delay itself is applied by whoever shows the lines. Subtitle files don't need it.
Video access units to keep queued, in seconds of frames. Set before [method open].

constants.constant: The whole file was read; what is queued can still be consumed. A [method seek] reads again.
